text:
I'll search the Obsidian vault and Hindsight memory for anything on Azure DevOps board structure before I answer.

I found several candidate files in the vault. Let me read the DevOps Analysis material and search Hindsight in parallel.

I have the DevOps Analysis folder. The Operating View HTML is the one that describes actual structure — let me extract the hierarchy sections from both HTML analyses.

Too much CSS noise. Let me strip the style blocks and pull just the body text.

This is exactly what Dom asked for. Let me pull the intake, roadmap, hierarchy and target-model sections — the "how we should use it" half.

Now the target operating model section — the "should" half of the ask.

You already have exactly this document — I don't need to build it from scratch. Here's what exists and the simple breakdown you asked for.

> 🧠 **From Hindsight memory (Inform Digital department strategy and roadmap)** — this connects to the active Digital department strategy/roadmap work for Erica, of which the DevOps operating model is the anchor.

**What we have** — `~/obsidian/Projects/Work/Inform/DevOps Analysis/`, filed 2026-08-25 from a full 5,426-item census (baseline 12 Aug 2026, so ~4 weeks stale now):

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| `Inform_Digital_Team_Operating_View.html` | **The main one.** As-is + target operating model, 10 sections |
| `..._Structure_and_Flow (superseded).html` | Earlier structural pass |
| `Copilot_Studio_Agents_..._OFGEM.html` | Separate ADO project, agent register |

**The hierarchy, top down.** Five streams share one project, one board set, one classification tree:

- **OWN** — Product Family → Product. 57 families, 421 products. The service/asset catalogue.
- **SELL** — Client → Statement of Work. 14 clients, 16 SoWs.
- **CHANGE** — Feature → PBI → Task. 659/1,328/2,244 items, 78% of the workspace. The best-run part.
- **RUN** — BAU → Task. 225 BAU, 700 children. Highest completion rate.
- **BUILD** — 16 repos → 8 builds → 2 releases.

**The verdict in three lines:** structure is right, discipline is uneven, feedback loop is missing. Seven ways in with no triage; 15% of items have no parent, 35% of open work no owner. A Task closes in 19 days, the Feature above it in 322 — that gap is waiting and not closing, not capacity.

**The six-point target model** to agree on: one front door (single intake type, weekly triage) · five named streams each with an owner and WIP limit · Now/Next/Later rolling roadmap replacing four competing iteration schemes · a definition of stale (60 days, monthly 30-min ritual) · work item ID into the build so the board knows what shipped · three config switches for controls.

Note the Product Family layer is already functioning as your roadmap theme layer, and WSJF is scored on 598 Features. You're one presentation change from a working roadmap, not one process change.

One thing to decide before you socialise this: the five parked workstreams (Autobots, Compliance and cyber, Copilot adoption, Copilot agents, Agent Log Lords — ~470 items, 30% of open backlog) are already ruled legacy in my notes, but the document still frames them as an open decision.

Want me to turn this into a one-page flow diagram or a short shareable summary for the ways-of-working conversation? The HTML is thorough but it's a 10-section read, not a thing you put in front of a team to agree on.
